newsitem.title: USA: Miami boy who turned in money gets reward.
newsitem.headline: Miami boy who turned in money gets reward.

text.p: Returning 85 cents that fell from a crashed armoured truck paid off for Herbert Tarvin Thursday, when he, his family and his sixth-grade class were given a free trip to Disney World.

Herbert, 11, was one of only two people who returned money scooped up by passers-by when a security firm's armoured truck crashed on an overpass last month, pouring millions of dollars in cash into an impoverished Miami neighbourhood below.

"I just hoped to do the right thing and turn the money in, because it doesn't belong to me," he told reporters after flying to Orlando with 27 relatives, classmates and teachers from St. Xavier Catholic School.

In an attempt to get back some of the estimated $550,000 still missing after the Jan. 8 crash, police declared two amnesties, during which those who had taken money could turn it in without fearing punishment.
Only a single mother of six, who turned in about $20 in quarters and pennies, and Herbert came forward. He gave the 85 cents to a teacher.
The trip was paid for by Disney and an airline.
